chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Elton Hill, Eddie Mallory and Hardy's Alabamans
summary: They discuss arranger Elton Hill, Eddie Mallory's band, and Marion Hardy's Alabamans, with whom Calloway first came to New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Now, we went on to some arrangers. We started talking about -- of course we mentioned Don and we mentioned Don Redmon and we mentioned Bennie Carter and
Fletcher Henderson and Horace Henderson. But there was a young kid that Tyree Glenn was with -- talking trombone players, we haven't mentioned. We haven't got to trombone players yet?
But we were mentioning about Elton Hale Hill.
Yes, I knew Elton Hill when he was with Tommy [Myles] in Washington and then later he was with Eddie Mallory at the same time --
Eddie Mallory was married to Ethel Waters --
-- and he was a musical conductor.
He come out with a band out -- Jimmy Wade's or one of those bands out of Chicago.
Uh-huh, yeah, and he was also with the Hardy's Alabamans, too.
Right, [must] have been with Hardy's Alabamans.
Coyle Les Corley was the guitar player.
And Doc Cheatham was in that band and Calloway conducted the band.
In fact that's the band that Calloway came to New York with first, --
